draft.title: Water balance in the body
card: The body must keep the water in its blood and cells within a narrow range. Water is gained from drink and food, and lost in urine, sweat and breath.
The hypothalamus detects when blood becomes too concentrated, for example after sweating or too little drink. It signals the pituitary gland to release more antidiuretic hormone (ADH) into the blood.
ADH acts on the kidneys. It makes them reabsorb more water back into the blood, so less water is lost and the urine is small in volume and concentrated.
When blood is too dilute, less ADH is released. The kidneys reabsorb less water, so more is lost in a large volume of dilute urine. This is negative feedback, as each change is reversed.
draft.remember: More ADH means more water kept and less urine. Less ADH means more water lost.

a.q: After a long run on a hot day, a student has sweated a lot and drunk little. What happens to ADH and urine?
opts: More ADH is released and urine is small and concentrated
More ADH is released and urine is large and dilute
Less ADH is released and urine is small and concentrated
Less ADH is released and urine is large and dilute
a.why: Sweating makes the blood more concentrated, so more ADH is released. ADH makes the kidneys reabsorb more water, so the urine is small and concentrated. Large, dilute urine would lose even more water and make the problem worse.
a.clue: The body needs to save water.

b.q: Liam drinks a large amount of water in a short time. His blood becomes more dilute. Which response restores water balance?
opts: Less ADH is released, so the kidneys reabsorb less water
Less ADH is released, so the kidneys reabsorb more water
More ADH is released, so the kidneys reabsorb less water
More ADH is released, so the kidneys reabsorb more water
b.why: Dilute blood has too much water, so ADH release falls. With less ADH the kidneys reabsorb less water and Liam passes more dilute urine. Releasing more ADH would keep water in the body and add to the excess.
b.clue: The response must reverse the change, so the body should lose water.

a.best: More ADH is released and urine is small and concentrated

b.best: Less ADH is released, so the kidneys reabsorb less water

problems.detail: The last bullet explains negative feedback ('This is negative feedback, as each change is reversed'). That idea belongs to point 1 and should only be mentioned here, not explained.

check.summary: The facts and both answers are correct, and the explanations match the card. One minor issue: the card briefly explains negative feedback, which belongs to point 1.
